[Help and Legend](general-information-legend)

PATIENTS WITH NEUTROPENIC FEVER WHO BECOME AFEBRILE IN THE FIRST 3 TO 5 DAYS OF

TREATMENT

# >>  Treatment if an INFECTIOUS CAUSE WAS IDENTIFIED and has resolved

(The infectious disease associated with the fever has resolved, the pathogen has

been controlled or eradicated, and the patient seems well)

Stop antimicrobials after treatment for pathogen/disease is completed, often

after 7 days.

# >>  Treatment if infectious cause of fever WAS NOT identified

To determine a patients risk level refer to

[Scoring tool to identify low risk febrile neutropenic patients](febrile-neutropenia-scoring-tool)

# Treatment for low risk patients

Consider a change to oral therapy

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h  \($0.18/day\) R,DI <AND> amoxicillin-](orz-set-abx-cipro-500mg-q12h-amox-clav-875-125-q12h)

clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h  ($1.56/day) [R]

# Treatment for high risk patients

Continue same antimicrobials for 7 days

[References](references)

Hughes WT Clin Infect Dis 2002, 34: 730

Rolston KVI Clin Infect Dis 2004, 39: S44
